transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I just don’t feel like doing anything anymore—not cooking, not music, not even playing dominoes with my friends. I used to love those things, but now I just don't have the spark to get up and do them.
Have you ever experienced a period of time where you felt unusually energetic, talkative, or productive, to the point where you didn't need much sleep or felt like you could do anything?

Yes, some weeks I'll wake up feeling like a motor that won't turn off, talking nonstop and cleaning the apartment or rearranging closets at midnight. I'll only sleep about two or three hours a night but still feel completely wired and full of energy. It is exhausting because my body just feels like it's being pushed from behind.
During those high-energy periods, did these behaviors cause significant disruption to your work or social life, or did you ever require hospitalization?

I've never been hospitalized, but these times have really disrupted my life and kept me from going to mass, choir, or the senior center anymore. It's gotten so bad that my daughter has had to take over managing my pills and bills because I get too confused or stuck to handle them myself.

During the periods when you feel low and lose interest in your hobbies, do you experience any thoughts that life is not worth living, or do you find yourself unable to take care of your basic needs like eating or hygiene?

No, I don't have thoughts of ending my life or anything like that. But I've completely stopped cooking and often just sit on the edge of the bed staring at the floor all day. I can't even handle simple household chores or my own medicine without getting stuck and confused, so my daughter has to do it all for me.
During those high-energy periods, did you ever experience a loss of touch with reality, such as believing you had special powers or hearing things that weren't actually there?

Yes, on those high-energy days I hear a man's voice calling my name and telling me I'm failing my mission, and I'm sure the neighbors are watching to test me. I also feel like God kept me alive to be a special messenger who could run the whole church better than the priest.

However, the patient's report of auditory hallucinations (hearing a voice) and delusions (believing they are a special messenger and that neighbors are monitoring them) during high-energy periods confirms the presence of psychotic features. According to ICD-10 criteria, the presence of psychotic symptoms during a manic episode necessitates the classification of F31.2 (Bipolar disorder, current episode manic with psychotic symptoms). F31.3 and F31.4 are no longer appropriate as they do not account for these severe psychotic features.
